title: Your backtest looks great, and that might be the problem

channel.name: Andrew Builds (TradeNotes)
channel.appBlurb: a trading journal and performance analytics app

body.hook: Your backtest looks great. That might be the problem.
body.promise: Three quiet errors can flatter a backtest. The third hides in plain sight.

beats.narration: Number one: look-ahead. The test used information you would not have had at that moment.
Number two: overfitting. Tune enough settings and almost any idea fits the past. And the past is all it fits.

scene.label: settings tried on the same data
scene.caption: One was always going to fit.

beats.narration: Number three, in plain sight: costs. Fees and slippage repeat on every single trade.

scene.title: Hypothetical backtest
scene.note: SAMPLE numbers. Hypothetical, not real results.

cards.label: Fees + slippage
cards.hint: Small per trade, on every trade.

beats.narration: Here is the part people skip. Even a clean backtest only describes history. It is not a forecast, and live trades can still lose money.

scene.sub: Risk of loss does not go away.

beats.narration: I built TradeNotes, my own trading journal, so I'm biased. It logs what you actually did, so you can hold it next to the test.
So a great backtest is not a finish line. It is a claim you still have to check.

body.cta: Before you trust a test, ask those three questions. Not financial advice.

promise.sub: The third hides in plain sight.

cta.title: TradeNotes
cta.tagline: Look-ahead, overfitting, costs. Ask all three before you trust a test.

post.ytDesc: Three quiet errors that can flatter a backtest: look-ahead, overfitting and missing costs. The numbers on screen are SAMPLE, hypothetical figures, not real results. A backtest describes what an idea did historically; it is not a prediction, and trading carries risk of loss. I built TradeNotes, so I'm biased. Educational content only, not financial advice.
